newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil posts $10.7 bln current account deficit.
newsitem.headline: Brazil posts $10.7 bln current account deficit.

text.p: Brazil posted a current account balance of payments deficit of $10.722 billion in the first four months of 1997, compared with a $5.181 billion gap in the January-April period last year, the Central Bank said.
The Central Bank did not give the value of the current account gap as a percentage of gross domestic product.
The bank said in a statement foreign direct investment in the first four months of 1997 reached $4.411 billion versus $1.746 billion in the same period last year.
The Central Bank also said net foreign reserves at the end of April stood at $55.288 billion, compared with $58.120 billion in March.
According to the international liquidity concept which includes accounts receivable, foreign reserves were $56.171 billion in April, down from $58.980 billion in March.

The bank said the increase in the current account deficit, which rose by nearly $4.0 billion in April, was mainly caused by Brazil's growing trade deficit which posted a roughly $4.0 billion shortfall in the first four months of the year.
In the first four months of 1996, Brazil posted a $300 million trade deficit, the Central Bank said.
The growing current account gap was also caused by a rising deficit in the services account which reached $7.6 billion between January and April compared $6.1 billion in the same period last year.

The services account deficit grew mainly because of an increase in dividends paid to overseas accounts which rose to $1.8 billion in the January-April period from $256 million in the same period last year.
